title: HB0011 (110th General Assembly): As enacted, enacts the "Tennessee Hearing Protection Act," which deletes the prohibition on possession, manufacture, transport, repair, or sale of a firearm silencer. - Amends TCA Section 39-17-1301 and Section 39-17-1302.

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, Tennessee); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Tennessee text (Chaptered, 2017-05-18; official copy via LegiScan getBillText doc 1801212)
provenance.note: Chaptered, Public Chapter 339, 2017-05-18 (Senate Bill 921 substituted for House Bill 11; one document). Quotes are instruction sentences; the bill deletes the silencer definition in 39-17-1301(5) and the offense in 39-17-1302(a)(5). Short title: "Tennessee Hearing Protection Act." SECTIONS 5-6 conform cross-references. Stop 1 (2026-11-14): Section 5 added to operative_text from the saved text; 39-17-1302(d) is the National Firearms Act compliance exception, so silencers (a)(5) and short-barrel guns (a)(4) were banned unless NFA-registered.

operative_text:
SECTION 2 (TCA 39-17-1301): is amended by deleting subdivision (5) in its entirety.
SECTION 3 (TCA 39-17-1302(a)(5)): is amended by deleting subdivision (aX5) in its entirety.
SECTION 4 (TCA 39-17-1302(c)(1)): is amended by deleting the language "(a)(1)-(5)" and substituting instead the language "(a)(1)-(4)".
SECTION 5 (TCA 39-17-1302(d)): is amended by deleting the language ", (a)(4), or (a)(5)" and substituting instead the language "or (aX4)".
